chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn 'Udhafir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on one of his journeys, a group of riders met him and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.' He turned to them and asked: 'Who are you?' They answered: 'We are believers.' He asked: 'What is the reality of your belief?' They replied: 'Contentment with the decree of Allah, submission to the command of Allah, and relinquishment of affairs to Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) responded: 'You are learned and wise; you are almost as wise as the prophets. If you are truthful, then do not build what you will not inhabit, do not collect what you will not eat, and fear Allah to whom you shall return.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say to believers about building and collecting wealth?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) distinguishes between mere theological submission to divine decree (*al-Rida*) and the practical wisdom required of true believers. He cautions against the accumulation of transient wealth and property, emphasizing that true faith manifests in detachment from the ephemeral world and readiness for the Hereafter. This highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating doctrinal acceptance with ethical conduct and spiritual mindfulness.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 12. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar said, on the authority of Muhamad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma`il ibn Bazi`, on the authority of Muhamad ibn `Udhafir, on the authority of his father that Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) said:

While the Messenger of Allah (SA) was on one of his journeys, some riders met him, and said: “Peace be upon you, O messenger of Allah.” So, he turned to them and asked, ”Who are you?” They answered, “We are believers.” He (SA) asked, “What is the nature of your belief?” They replied, “Pleasure in the destiny of Allah, submission to the command of Allah, and relinquishment to Allah (of all affairs).” The Messenger of Allah (SA) responded, “You are learned and wise. You are almost as wise as the prophets. If you are truthful, then do not build what you will not inhabit, do not collect what you will not eat, and fear Allah to whom you shall return.”
